1.title: Exam Technique: Scenarios, Matching Questions and the Open Book
1.text: Welcome to Module seventeen: Exam Technique: Scenarios, Matching Questions and the Open Book. Each part of this module comes from the study notes of the same name, so you can read the notes after you watch.

1.title: What You Will Learn
1.text: By the end of this module you will be able to do six things. The two question types, the marking and the time plan. A method for scenario questions. Using the open book quickly. Choosers: which process or practice, and who decides. Look-alike terms. Practice with exam-style questions and a recall check.

1.title: Where This Fits in the Exam
1.text: Here is where this module sits in the exam. Scope: All learning outcomes: method, chooser tables and look-alike terms. Exam format: an open-book scenario exam: one hundred fifty minutes, seventy marks, forty-two marks to pass. Validated against: the official prince two seven Practitioner syllabus (people cert), version seven point two.

1.title: The two question types, the marking and the time plan
1.text: The two question types, the marking and the time plan. The exam is open book, lasts one hundred fifty minutes (one hundred eighty-eight with extra time) and has seventy marks. You need forty-two to pass. There is no negative marking, so answer every question. The questions test applying the method (level three) and analyzing whether an action is effective (level four).

1.title: The two question types, the marking and the time plan, continued
1.text: The two question types, the marking and the time plan. Marks. Classic question: one. Matching question: three, one for each of the three parts. Layout. Classic question: A short situation, one question, four options A to D. Matching question: Three pieces of information, each matched to one of five or six options. Options. Classic question: Choose one. Matching question: Each option can be used once, more than once or not at all. Each part of a matching question is marked on its own, so never leave a part blank.

1.title: The two question types, the marking and the time plan, continued
1.text: The two question types, the marking and the time plan. Read the scenario and the Additional Information once. one hundred fifty minutes: five. one hundred eighty-eight minutes: six. First pass: answer everything, flag doubts. one hundred fifty minutes: one hundred twenty. one hundred eighty-eight minutes: one hundred fifty. Review flagged questions with the book. one hundred fifty minutes: twenty. one hundred eighty-eight minutes: twenty-seven. Final check: no blanks. one hundred fifty minutes: five. one hundred eighty-eight minutes: five. Exam tip: In a matching question, options can repeat. If two parts have the same answer, that is allowed.

1.title: A method for scenario questions
1.text: A method for scenario questions. Work in the same order every time. Read the question line first, so you know what is asked. Read the scenario for the facts: stage, who acts, what changed, tolerances. For "was this appropriate", decide Yes or No first, then choose the reason that fits the facts. Cross out options that break a rule, for example the board deciding inside tolerance. If two options remain, confirm in the book, then move on. Ask five questions in every scenario.

1.title: A method for scenario questions, continued
1.text: A method for scenario questions. one. Where are we? The process, the stage and the practice. two. Who is acting? The role and its authority, including tolerances. three. What changed? An issue, a risk, a forecast breach or a request. four. Which rule applies? A principle, a practice rule or the process purpose. five. Does it fit this project? Size, delivery method, the people and tailoring.

1.title: A method for scenario questions, continued
1.text: A method for scenario questions. The Additional Information about people: at least one question needs it. When a question names a person or group, find them there first. Note their role, experience, attitude and workload. Then choose the action that fits that person, such as a short conversation for a busy executive. Exam tip: For "was this appropriate", pick Yes or No first, then the reason that matches the scenario facts.

1.title: Using the open book quickly
1.text: Using the open book quickly. Only the Official Book is allowed, and you may annotate it. Use it to confirm, not to learn: about thirty seconds a look-up, then flag and move on. Role tables of each practice (Tables five point one, six point four, seven point one, eight point two, nine point three, ten point two, eleven point three). Areas of focus for each role. Process tables (Chapters thirteen to nineteen: activities, roles, practices applied, inputs and outputs). Who does what in each process. Management product descriptions. What each product is for and who receives it. The index. A fast route to any term. Write your own page index on the inside cover and highlight the role tables.

1.title: Choosers: which process or practice, and who decides
1.text: Choosers: which process or practice, and who decides. Mandate, appoint executive and project manager, project brief. Starting up a project. Board gives authority or ad hoc direction; closure authorized. Directing a project. Baseline the P I D, approaches and plans before major spend. Initiating a project. Authorize and monitor work packages; highlight report. Controlling a stage. Accept and deliver a work package; checkpoint report. Managing product delivery. End stage report, next stage plan, business case update. Managing a stage boundary. Acceptance, handover, end project report, benefits review plan. Closing a project.

1.title: Choosers: which process or practice, and who decides, continued
1.text: Choosers: which process or practice, and who decides. Why, benefits, value. Business case. Roles, team structure, suppliers. Organization. Plans, tolerances, work packages. Plans. Acceptance criteria, reviews, quality register. Quality. Threat, opportunity, appetite. Risk. Change request, problem, off-specification. Issues. Reports, forecasts, exceptions, lessons. Progress.

1.title: Choosers: which process or practice, and who decides, continued
1.text: Choosers: which process or practice, and who decides. Corporate or programme level. Project tolerances and mandate; receives lessons. Project board. Authorizes initiation, the project, each stage, exception plans, closure; sets stage tolerances. Project manager. Day-to-day control; authorizes work packages; corrective action inside tolerance. Team manager. Agrees and delivers a work package. Change authority. Approves or rejects changes inside its delegated authority. Project assurance. Checks independently and advises; does not decide for others.

1.title: Look-alike terms
1.text: Look-alike terms. Checkpoint report and highlight report. Team manager to project manager on a work package; project manager to board on the stage. Exception report and exception plan. The report warns the board of a forecast breach; the plan replaces the plan being exceeded. End stage, end project and lessons reports. One stage ending; the whole project against its baselines; lessons for others. Project brief and P I D. The start-up view; the baseline from initiation. Business case and benefits management approach. Why the project is justified; how benefits are measured and reviewed.

2.title: Look-alike terms, continued
2.text: Look-alike terms. Issue register and issue report. The log of all issues; the detail of one issue. Risk register and risk management approach. The list of risks and status; how risk will be managed. Product description, project product description, work package description. One product; the whole project product; work given to a team manager. Exam tip: When two terms look alike, ask who sends it, who receives it and what it covers. Level and audience separate almost every pair.

2.title: Practice Question 1
2.text: Question one. Project Harbor's build stage has a time tolerance of plus or minus two weeks. Sam Okafor forecasts a delay of three weeks but plans to mention it at the next highlight report in four weeks. Was this an appropriate action for the project manager to take, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is B: No, because a forecast breach of tolerance must be escalated promptly. A forecast breach is an exception that goes to the board promptly (manage by exception).

2.title: Practice Question 2
2.text: Question two. Project Harbor receives a request for a small extra reporting screen. The board delegated small changes to Tomas Reyes within a set budget, and this change fits inside it. Who decides whether to approve the change? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: Tomas Reyes, as change authority. The change authority decides changes inside the authority the board delegated (issues practice).

2.title: Practice Question 3
2.text: Question three. Tomas Reyes, the harbor master, prefers brief face-to-face updates and rarely reads long documents. Sam Okafor must keep him informed during the build stage. What should Sam do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Agree a short regular conversation, backed by brief reports. Communication should fit the person, so Sam adapts the channel and still keeps him informed.

2.title: Practice Question 4
2.text: Question four. Sam wants Wei Chen's team to have a clear statement of the work, the product, the tolerances and the reporting for the next three weeks. Which management product should Sam give Wei? The four options are on the screen. The answer is D: A work package description for the work. The work package description hands work from the project manager to a team manager.

2.title: Practice Question 5
2.text: Question five. Sam hears that the pilot testers may be unavailable in June. Nothing has happened yet, but it could delay the pilot stage. What should Sam do? The four options are on the screen. The answer is A: Record it in the risk register, assess it and plan a response. Something that might happen is a risk, so it belongs in the risk register.

2.title: Practice Question 6
2.text: Question six. The board decides to stop Project Harbor early because the port's budget has been cut. Sam Okafor starts managing a stage boundary to plan a final stage. Was this an appropriate action for the project manager to take, and why? The four options are on the screen. The answer is C: No, because an early stop is handled through closing a project. Stopping early is a premature close, handled by closing a project.

2.title: Recall Check 1
2.text: Recall check one. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question one. How many marks are needed to pass, and out of how many? Answer: forty-two out of seventy. Question two. How long is the exam, and how long with extra time? Answer: one hundred fifty minutes, or one hundred eighty-eight minutes with extra time. Question three. How is a matching question marked? Answer: Three marks, one for each part, and options can be used once, more than once or not at all.

2.title: Recall Check 2
2.text: Recall check two. Say each answer out loud before you listen to mine. Question four. What are the five questions to ask in every scenario? Answer: Where are we, who is acting, what changed, which rule applies and does it fit this project. Question five. Which material is allowed in the exam? Answer: The Official Book, which you may annotate, and nothing else. Question six. Which two levels of thinking does the exam test? Answer: Applying the method (level three) and analyzing whether an action is effective (level four).

2.title: Module Recap
2.text: Here is the recap. Exam: open book, one hundred fifty minutes (one hundred eighty-eight with extra time), seventy marks, pass forty-two. Question types: classic: one mark, A to D; matching: three marks, options can repeat. Time plan: five to read, one hundred twenty first pass, twenty review, five final check. Method: question line first, Yes or No first, cross out rule breakers. Five questions: where, who, what changed, which rule, does it fit. Open book: tab role and process tables; confirm, do not learn. Look-alikes: who sends it, who receives it, what it covers. If this course is helping you, please subscribe to the channel and hit the bell icon, so you get a notification when the next video is out. That completes the course. Good luck with the exam.
